key_insight: The paper turns Gaussian entanglement and communication limits into tractable convex-optimization problems with provable convergence and polynomial-time bit complexity for fixed rational covariance inputs.
engineering_relevance: It provides computable upper bounds on quantum, private, and key-distribution performance for noisy optical links, useful for designing and benchmarking continuous-variable quantum communication systems.
method: Develops Gaussian-restricted relative entropy of entanglement and Rains entanglement via an integral representation and matrix geometric means.
Derives unique optimal reference states, additivity for independent Gaussian inputs, and a convex-majorization algorithm with explicit convergence guarantees.
Uses teleportation simulation, energy allocation, and passive-basis loss-core optimization to bound two-way assisted communication rates under energy constraints.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports explicit geometric convergence, polynomial bit-complexity for fixed rational covariance matrices, and numerical two- and three-mode examples that match known pure-loss benchmarks.
watch_item: The strongest complexity and convergence guarantees are for Gaussian-restricted or fixed rational-input settings, while unrestricted quantities require photon-number truncation with controlled but nontrivial approximation error.
paper_title: Gaussian entanglement and quantum communication: geodesic optimization and multimode bounds
